## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe observes one fitted BERT4Rec category model through `ModelView`; model implementation details are not supplied. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)`. Prefix inference uses left-padded histories ending in a reserved MASK. The user representation is the feature at the greatest nonpadding position—the appended MASK—never `count-1`.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, plus training histories and optional aligned timestamps. Metadata references are retained, but item categories and reviews are unavailable.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with aligned `B × L` tensors. Feature and scoring calls prefer network methods, falling back to view methods. Diagnosis runs in evaluation mode without gradients, restoring module modes and captured RNG states afterward; iterator progress and worker-local RNGs cannot be restored.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding similarity:** Samples up to 2,048 real-item embeddings, excluding PAD/MASK. Mean off-diagonal cosine is mapped to `[0,1]`; higher values indicate greater angular similarity, not necessarily poor recommendation diversity. Fewer than two embeddings yields null.
- **Supervised separation:** Reads at most ten batches and scores only supervised MASK positions with valid positive/negative IDs. Reports mean margin, tenth-percentile margin, negative-beats-positive rate and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower failure rates indicate stronger sampled training separation. Audits count excluded positions; category lists remain empty.
- **Prefix dependence:** Samples up to 200 training users, treating the final training event as target. Scores that target against 99 fixed unique negatives. Reports rank, descriptive HR@10, raw/standardized margins and top-10 overlap.

# Perturbation & Tests

Frozen prefixes undergo identity copying, compact deletion of recent/oldest events, ten random deletions and ten recent-order permutations. Readout remains at MASK. Identity scores must reproduce within tolerance.

Edited-minus-baseline effects are averaged within user, then across users, with exploratory paired-user bootstrap intervals. Reports include no-ops, effective edits, strata and optional timestamp inversions. Positive HR/margin deltas indicate improvement; positive rank deltas indicate degradation. Sensitivity alone establishes neither usefulness nor causality.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, covering embedding similarity, supervised margins/audits and nested `recent_history_probe` results. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` requests a grounded JSON interpretation with status, findings, implications and evidence.

Prefix results are in-sample diagnostics, not host validation performance. Held-out usefulness, four-category macro effects, position-preserving deletion, release availability and simulator traits remain unmeasured. Missing evidence must remain explicit.


 ## Search results
Search found relevant intervention methods, but no directly verified 2024–2026 BERT4Rec activation-patching study. [Zhang and Nanda, ICLR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) show that corruption methods and evaluation metrics can substantially change localization results. [Heimersheim and Nanda, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255) distinguish restoration from disruption experiments and caution against interpreting either as complete circuit identification. A [RecSys 2026 study](https://programs.sigchi.org/recsys/2026/program/content/264578) investigates last-item reliance through residual scaling, but concerns causal self-attention; transfer to bidirectional BERT4Rec remains a hypothesis.

Suggested synthesis: freeze one checkpoint; compare recent-item substitutions against equally sized older-item substitutions, matching replacement popularity using training counts. Separately intervene on positional embeddings while preserving item identities, padding and attention masks. Patch clean attention-head outputs, residual streams and MLP outputs into corrupted runs; reverse patch direction to test disruption. Controls: identity patches, unrelated-user donor activations, matched random heads and whole-layer restoration as a pipeline positive control. Measure target-versus-fixed-negative score margins, rank changes and HR@10; report paired uncertainty. Attention weights alone cannot establish component causality.

Popularity dependence is plausible: [PrePRec, RecSys 2024](https://sundaram.cs.illinois.edu/pubs/2024/2024_wang_pretrained.pdf) reports stronger SASRec/BERT4Rec performance on popular items. Stratify intervention effects by target popularity and history length; score–frequency correlation alone does not establish a shortcut. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-item formulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690): append the reserved MASK, read its final nonpadding position, and exclude the target from bidirectional input. Compare internal-mask reconstruction with appended-mask prediction to investigate supervision mismatch, explicitly labeling training-prefix results as training-exposed evidence. These are proposed probes, not published BERT4Rec findings.

Sampled HR@10 measures ranking within the chosen candidate distribution; it need not preserve full-catalog model ordering, even in expectation. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish this inconsistency. [Pereira et al., RecSys 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examine sampling reliability under differing exposure conditions, distinguishing resolution, fidelity, robustness and predictive power. Implication: margins against 99 sampled negatives and perturbation sensitivity are diagnostic hypotheses, not established measures of catalog-wide ranking quality. Preserve the pinned host evaluator for selection.

[Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find that average sequential-recommendation performance can hide substantial head/mid/tail differences; training-negative strategies trade overall accuracy against popularity balance. Suggested auxiliary audit: use each category’s single checkpoint to score the full unseen catalog for the designated training users; report recommendation coverage, training-frequency distribution and concentration. Without held-out relevance labels, these describe exposure, not accuracy. Where validation labels are available, stratify hits and target ranks by training-only item frequency, repeat status and history length. Separate repeat targets from unseen-item audits, whose exclusion rule otherwise removes them.

Bootstrap methods support uncertainty assessment for retrieval metrics ([Sakai](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ipsjdc/3/0/3_0_625/_article/-char/en)). Proposed application: when host per-user outcomes are available, resample paired users within each category, preserve identical candidates across compared checkpoints, and recompute the four-category macro HR@10 difference and confidence interval. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates; it does not remove candidate bias or repeated-search selection bias. Report stratum counts and assess diagnostic–validation associations only from observed host outputs; twenty audited training users cannot establish generalization.

Recent work supports separating semantic relatedness from user preference. *Disentangling Likes and Dislikes* (2024/WWW 2025) finds that strong textual-similarity scores do not ensure explanations reflect users’ positive or negative opinions; its review-based supervision is unavailable here, so only its evaluation distinction transfers. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13248). *Beyond Explicit and Implicit* (2025), based on interviews with 34 users, distinguishes feedback intentions from observable consumption behavior—supporting caution when interpreting interactions as immediate desire or rejection. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09869).

Suggested diagnostic protocol, synthesized from these findings: annotate explicit immediate choice, broad relatedness, explicit rejection, and insufficient evidence separately; record redundancy as an additional flag. Require supporting feedback excerpts or history/item references, document temporal scope, and leave ownership, compatibility and mood unknown unless stated. Independently double-code a sample; report raw agreement, nominal Krippendorff’s alpha, label counts and adjudicated disagreements. The 2025 HCI+NLP proceedings recommend recording evidence/reasoning to support disagreement review and discuss agreement measures. [Proceedings](https://aclanthology.org/2025.hcinlp-1.pdf).

For automated annotation, *Trust or Escalate* (ICLR 2025) calibrates judge-confidence thresholds against human labels to control disagreement while retaining coverage. Adaptation: calibrate on separate human annotations; report coverage, error among accepted judgments and risk–coverage curves.
